To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the use of a letter as a rhetorical form in Anzalduan texts is an effective strategy for challenging Euro‐American readers to rethink their approach and that the use of the letter form is consistent with the embodiment approach to rhetoric.
the letter is a distinct form of rhetoric and that the letter is an embodied rhetorical form that enables the author to create an embodied space in which the audience is not addressed.
The letter is a unique form of communication.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: How can we understand the rhetorical effects of Anzalda’s letter?
the ways in which the body is represented and understood in the field of rhetoric and communication.
the question, “How do people of color use language in ways that are not understood by Euro‐Americans?”
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Anzaldúa is not only a Chicana feminist writer but also a rhetorician.
Anzaldúa uses the form of a letter to create an embodied rhetorical approach to the writing of texts by people of colour.

Gloria Anzaldua's letter “Speaking in tongues” is a rhetorical masterpiece that is worthy of our attention, and that it is a text that challenges Euro‐Americans to reexamine their approach to texts written by people of color, and that the rhetorical form of the letter is a distinct genre that enables an author, in this case Gloria Anzaldú, to address an audience in a manner that is both intimate and personal.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Anzalduas letter is a text that is both an argument and a letter, a text that is simultaneously an argument and a personal message.
we are interested in the ways in which the body, the border, and the letter can help us to rethink the ways in which we approach the texts of people of color.
we have shown that the letter is a distinct form of writing that enables the author to address a specific audience and to suspend the non addressed audience in an aporetic position.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the body is not a static object that can be understood through a single lens, but is instead an ever changing entity that can be understood in multiple ways.

the rhetorical form of the letter enables the author to address the non‐addressing audience in a way that allows them to be suspended from the text, to be a critical audience, and to be an audience that is not addressed.
the letter is a form of communication that is particularly useful in the context of a borderland.
